headline: Microsoft beat and our 3-month call flipped green before the bell, Alphabet got hit for 10%, T-Mobile is up too, and no Bold Bet again because nothing on Thursday's board cleared Max Edge's bar
top_call: Microsoft beat, and our 3-month call flipped to the right side of the S&P 500 before the bell. Azure grew 48%, earnings came in at $4.89 a share vs $4.73 expected, and the stock traded near $543 premarket, about 1.2 points ahead of the S&P after closing Wednesday 1.2 points behind. Alphabet dropped 10% on the same AI spending story. Very different report cards.
backdrop: Nasdaq futures fell about 1% early Thursday after Alphabet's negative free cash flow revived worries about AI spending, with Alphabet down 10.2% premarket and Microsoft up 3.6% on a cloud-driven beat. The Fed held rates on Wednesday; Amazon and Intel report after Thursday's close.

ai.headline: Alphabet slides 10% premarket after negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion, while Microsoft rises on capex below forecasts
ai.why: Wall Street just stopped grading AI spending on a curve: spend big, fine, but show the cash.

ai.headline: Google DeepMind announces Gemini 4 Carbon, ranked first on Artificial Analysis's index, but only select cyber defenders can use it for now
ai.why: The best model on the leaderboard is behind a velvet rope, and that's the new normal for cyber-capable AI.

ai.headline: The US Justice Department is asking how Nvidia's $12.93 billion Hugging Face deal would affect competition in AI
ai.why: Owning the chips and the place everyone downloads models from is the kind of combo antitrust lawyers circle in red.

ai.headline: Microsoft booked $10 billion of revenue from OpenAI deals in one quarter, nearly 11% of its $92.3 billion total
ai.why: OpenAI is now a bigger business line for Microsoft than Bing or Xbox, which is a sentence nobody predicted in 2019.

ai.headline: Axiom says swarms of AI agents helped formalize math's longest proof, the classification of finite simple groups, in Lean in 24 days
ai.why: About 15,000 pages of human proof, machine-checked line by line, and it even turned up 34 notable deviations along the way.
